verified.presentation.enterFullscreen: same control as controls.fullscreen (long-standing .ytp-* player chrome)
verified.presentation.enterTheater: .ytp-size-button is the player chrome theater/default toggle; unverified 2026-09-01 that it reads as theater when already in theater (the keeper only fires after a drop, so it toggles INTO theater)
verified.presentation.play: state-conditioned on the button aria-label (Play / Replay) so it never pauses; English UI
verified.videoLibrary: read live 2026-10-11 on a hidden muted page, signed in: /playlist?list=WL lists ytd-playlist-video-renderer (a#video-title, ytd-channel-name a, ytd-thumbnail img, the duration badge); /feed/history lists ytd-video-renderer the same way, the resume bar ytd-thumbnail-overlay-resume-playback-renderer #progress NOT seen (the first thirty were Shorts); /feed/channels lists 53 ytd-channel-renderer (a#main-link /@handle, #channel-title, #video-count 'N subscribers', img); the sidebar's subscriptions section is the ytd-guide-section-renderer whose first entry is /feed/subscriptions, its entries /@handle with a ytd-guide-collapsible-entry-renderer 'Show more'. /feed/subscriptions (yt-lockup-view-model) is read but not used yet. Artwork falls back to i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg (the page leaves off-screen thumbnails empty); Shorts are left out of Continue watching (nothing to resume). /feed/subscriptions (yt-lockup-view-model: h3 a, yt-content-metadata-view-model rows 'Channel N views N ago', the duration badge) read live 2026-10-11 as the own row 'Latest from your subscriptions', in the owned walk. Continue watching = the history items YouTube's own bar marks part-watched (2% to 95%, the bar div[class*=ResumePlaybackRendererThumbnailOverlayResumePlayback] style width, read 2026-10-11); a finished video (full bar) or one with no bar is not a continue ("What if I just finished it?"). The history page is scrolled up to four times when fewer than 12 videos (Shorts aside) are listed.
verified.videoContext: UNVERIFIED 2026-10-11: written from the player's known classes (#movie_player, .html5-main-video, ad-showing, ytd-watch-metadata h1, #owner ytd-channel-name); not played on this account. 2026-10-12 ('The video finishes and then the screen goes to the youtube page'): at the end #movie_player carries ended-mode and the player can lose its clock, which read as a stopped player (the doctor replayed the clip); the context now reports the end as not playing at the full length (the length last seen), so core's at-end rule stands and Watch comes back.
verified.videoCmd: UNVERIFIED 2026-10-11: .ytp-play-button, .ytp-next-button, .ytp-subtitles-button, .ytp-fullscreen-button, and the video element's own time for ten seconds either way (YouTube's player is a plain HTML5 video, unlike Netflix's); no skipintro, so a skip is the person's own press. 2026-10-12 fullscreen: pressed before the watch page's app has drawn (ytd-watch-flexy with its video-id comes ~1.8 s after the load event, read on a hidden page) the button puts the document in fullscreen with the page's own layout still drawn (comments beside the picture); the command answers false until the app is there, and the stage loop asks again. 2026-10-12 live chat: a stream's chat (ytd-live-chat-frame, live or replay) stays open beside the fullscreen player in YouTube's full-bleed layout (the player 1744 of 2400 px, the chat frame 655), read on a stream replay; the frame's own header Close button, inside its same-origin iframe#chatframe, collapses it (the frame gains collapsed + hide-chat-frame) and the player fills the window; pressed before the fullscreen control, once, while the frame is open.
verified.purchaseProviders: TMDB/JustWatch's YouTube provider id 192, read live 2026-10-11 from a title's Rent and Buy offers (not a subscription: tmdbProviders stays unset).
verified.videoListSet: Watch later's Remove read live 2026-10-11 on the hidden page: each ytd-playlist-video-renderer's ytd-menu-renderer button opens a popup whose ytd-menu-service-item-renderer reads 'Remove from Watch later' (seen, not pressed: nothing was removed from the household's list). Adding, on the watch page's Save and its Watch later checkbox, is UNVERIFIED.
verified.videoChannelInfo: read live 2026-10-11 on a public channel's /videos page: yt-page-header-view-model h1, yt-description-preview-view-model with a '...more' button, yt-avatar-shape img, the grid's yt-lockup-view-model items (h3 a, the duration badge). The counts' metadata rows and the unfolded description (ytd-about-channel-renderer) were not confirmed. The channel's Videos tab is the page read (videoChannelPage): its home tab is shelves and lists no videos, so a read of it gave no latest (found from the phone, 2026-10-11).
verified.videoPool: videoPool: /results?search_query=%23space, the Recently uploaded chip (yt-chip-cloud-chip-renderer) pressed on the hidden page, ytd-video-renderer cards (a#video-title, ytd-channel-name a, #metadata-line spans views + 'N ago', the time-status badge) read live 2026-10-11. The sp= sort parameter is ignored on a signed-in page, so the chip is the filter.
verified.videoTagsFetch: watch/<id> (no query string) answers an anonymous GET with the page's keywords meta, the creator's own tags, checked 2026-10-11 with Prism's agent string.
verified.videoRemoveContinue: /feed/history: each ytd-video-renderer's Action menu (button[aria-label='Action menu']) opens a ytd-menu-popup-renderer whose last entry is 'Remove from watch history', read 2026-10-11 on the hidden page and closed with Escape, not pressed.
verified.videoEpisodes: 2026-10-12 ('the episode lists for the SNL ones dont match up to what the youtube channel actually provides'): a video's Episodes are its channel's Videos tab (/@handle/videos, ytd-rich-item-renderer cards as the channel reader parses them), one season 'Latest videos' numbered so the newest is last; without it the series name (the channel's) went to TMDB, which knows Saturday Night Live the show. context.channel is the owner link's path (@handle, channel/UC..., c/..., user/...).

notes: §26 presentation actions are invocable ONLY through core presentation keeper (a standing per-assignment instruction); nothing else in core or the shell reads the presentation block. || YouTube as a Video player service (2026-10-11): Watch later is the list (My list), History is Continue watching, the subscribed channels are the service's own row 'Subscriptions' (the sidebar on every page read, the All subscriptions page as the six-hourly owned walk, which completes at once), as Twitch's followed channels are. A channel card opens the channel's page. No videoSearch yet: Search everywhere does not reach YouTube, its own search page does. The ads script (js) is the extension's signal. Nothing here reads an account or settings page. || Watch later's Remove (2026-10-11): the list page's own item menu. A channel card (videoChannelInfo): the channel's page read for its name, description, counts and latest videos, with a search of that channel's content (/@handle/search?query=).
